harmonicFunction: A (I) - Resonant, open major tonic establishing triumphant Australian road-song energy
D (IV) - Major subdominant providing expansive harmonic breathing room
E (V) - Dominant delivering classic blues-rock tension before the turnaround
G (♭VII) - Mixolydian borrowed chord injecting raw rock defiance and melodic drive

techniques.name: Driving Blues Shuffle Chug & Palm Muting
techniques.description: High-energy straight-eighth boogie shuffle groove driven by root-fifth and root-sixth power chord stretches with percussive right-hand palm muting

notes: A5/A6: 0-2-X-X-X-X alternating with 0-4-X-X-X-X
D5/D6: X-0-2-X-X-X alternating with X-0-4-X-X-X
E5/E6: 0-2-X-X-X-X on low E alternating with 0-4-X-X-X-X
sequence: Rest the palm heel lightly across the bridge saddles for tight low-end chug
Drive continuous eighth notes at 128 BPM locking with the bass and drums
Unmute sharply on the G major chord accents to give the shuffle dramatic push
tips: Keep the fret hand thumb hooked over the top of the neck for fretboard anchor stability
Use a Stratocaster bridge pickup or bridge/middle for punchy rhythm cut
Don't drag the tempo; maintain aggressive Australian pub rock forward drive

techniques.name: Ian Moss Soulful Vocal Bends & Pentatonic Blending
techniques.description: Ian Moss's signature lead guitar approach: seamlessly blending A major pentatonic (sweet C# 3rd) with A minor pentatonic (gritty C natural), weeping whole-step overbends, and singing vocal sustain

notes: Target sweet C# major 3rd at 14th fret G string and 11th fret D string
Full whole-step bends at 7th fret G string (D up to E) and 17th fret high E string
Punchy double stops at 5th fret strings 1 & 2, and 14th fret strings 2 & 3
sequence: Establish high presence on the neck pickup of a cranked valve amplifier
Begin with sparse vocal-like phrasing before exploding into high-register blues runs
Apply wide, slow, singing finger vibrato to every sustained note
tips: Select the Stratocaster neck single-coil for warm, woody, singing sustain
Dig in hard with the pick edge to make the initial transient pop like a horn stab
Leave dynamic breathing space between phrases to let the rhythm section surge

sections.name: Intro Slow-Burn Electric Piano & Guitar Chime
sections.technique: Open Ringing Chords & Subtle Lead Fills
sections.description: Don Walker's electric piano sets the moody Australian heartland scene, answered by Ian Moss's warm ringing open chords.
notes: Play with gentle, ringing dynamics as the band builds atmosphere
Let the open high E and B strings shimmer across the A and D shapes
Hit the G major chord decisively on the turnaround

sections.name: Driving Rhythm Shuffle & Verse 1
sections.technique: Driving Blues Shuffle Chug & Palm Muting
sections.description: The band locks into the unmistakable 128 BPM pub rock shuffle underneath Ian Moss's passionate lead vocal.
notes: Tight palm muting on the root-fifth and root-sixth power chord stretches
Keep the eighth-note picking steady and unyielding
Open up the muting on the chord changes

sections.name: Chorus Anthem 'Money in My Pocket'
sections.description: Explosive singalong chorus ('I got the money in my pocket, I got the need to get away') with ringing open chords.
notes: Lift all muting and strike full open chords across all six strings
Drive the A to D transition with maximum downstroke punch
Accent the G major subtonic lift into the turnaround

sections.name: Bridge Minor Descent & Tension Build
sections.description: Introspective minor detour ('Any other day I would have held you...') stepping through F#m, D, E, and C before launching the solo.
notes: Barre the 2nd fret cleanly for the F#m chord
Crescendo on the C major borrowed flat-III chord
Set up the explosive entrance of Ian Moss's guitar solo

sections.name: Ian Moss's Legendary Stratocaster Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Ian Moss Soulful Vocal Bends & Pentatonic Blending
sections.description: Widely hailed as one of the greatest Australian rock solos of all time. Moss blends stinging A minor blues aggression with sweet A major pentatonic chord tones, weeping whole-step bends at the 7th fret of the G string and 17th fret of the high E, and soulful phrasing that sings with unmatched vocal expression.
notes: Start on the high E string at fret 5 with vocal-like blues phrasing
Execute a crying whole-step bend on the 7th fret G string with slow vibrato
Ascend into the high 14th/17th fret register over the E-to-G chords
Climax with a screaming 17th-fret whole-step bend and fluid double-stop resolution

sections.name: Outro Jam & Dual-Guitar Power Climax
sections.description: The band enters full arena overdrive, with Ian Moss delivering furious high-register blues licks as the rhythm section gallops to the final crashing chord.
sections.progression: A - D - E - G (repeating to final crash)
notes: Maintain maximum downstroke power on the repeating A - D - E - G cadence
Weave screaming bends at the 17th and 19th frets of the high E string
Hit the final sustained A chord with roaring Marshall power-tube overdrive

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster (Ian Moss signature / 1960s reissue with maple fretboard)
guitar.pickup: Stratocaster neck single-coil pickup for signature fat, woody, expressive blues sustain

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 50-watt / Fender Super Reverb cranked into power tube saturation

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS808 / TS9 Tube Screamer boosting a cranked Marshall valve amp
effects.other: Boss CE-2 chorus on clean chord intros for classic 1980s Australian pub atmosphere
effects.delay: Short tape delay providing room ambience and solo bloom

beginner.title: Shuffle Chords & Rhythm Foundation
steps: Learn open A, D, and E chords and the standard 2-finger pub rock shuffle pattern
Practice playing clean downstrokes at 100 BPM locking with a metronome
Learn the chorus chord progression including the borrowed G major chord

intermediate.title: Major & Minor Pentatonic Vocabulary
steps: Learn the 5th-position A major and A minor pentatonic scale shapes side-by-side
Practice targeting the major 3rd (C#) on A chords and the minor 3rd (C) for blues tension
Develop an accurate full-step bend on the G and B strings with steady finger vibrato

advanced.title: Ian Moss Solo Transcription & Nuance
steps: Transcribe and perform Ian Moss's complete multi-stage guitar solo
Master the expressive vocal nuances, micro-bends, and dynamic pick attacks
Perform the solo with full physical emotion, holding sustain without unwanted string feedback

commonMistakes: Playing strictly minor pentatonic, missing Ian Moss's sweet, singing major pentatonic notes
Over-compressing the guitar tone, killing the natural touch dynamics between soft picking and hard digs
Rushing ahead of the rhythm section during the solo instead of sitting in the blues pocket
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: A major and A minor pentatonic switching drills at the 5th fret
15 minutes: Metronome shuffle practice locking downbeats at 128 BPM
15 minutes: Full-step and half-step bending intonation practice with digital tuner
focusAreas: Sweet major 3rd (C#) targeting over A chords
Neck-pickup Stratocaster tone and touch sensitivity
Dynamic patience during blues solo builds
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 128 BPM and practice landing the shuffle chug precisely on the upbeat eighth notes
